messages.subject: using ddply but preserving some of the outside data
messages.subject_clean: using ddply but preserving some of the outside data
messages.body_plain:
I recently asked this question in r-help, and while I got an answer
(http://www.nabble.com/using-ddply-but-preserving-some-of-the-outside-
data-td24834295.html ), it was neither as elegant nor as flexible as I
would like - and I suspect there is a better cleaner solution.

I'm working with a data set for which I    have sampled sites at a
variety of dates.  I want to use this data,   and get a running
average of the sampled values for the current and  previous date.  I
also note that, I have a vareity of other datasets where dates are not
quite so continuous, or I'm trying to use more complex functions than
a simple running average (for example, a running variance, or other
transformation - hence, the zoo library's running mean function isn't
going to work exactly for me).

I originally thought something like ddply would be ideal for this,
however, I cannot break up my data by date, and then apply a function
that requires information about the previous dates.

I had thought to use a for loop and merge, but that doesn't quite
seem  to be working.

So, my questions are twofold

1) Is there a way to use something like the plyr library to do this
efficiently
        1a) Indeed, is there a way to use ddply or its ilk to have a
function
that returns a vector of values, and then assign the variables you
are
sorting by to the whole vector?  Or maybe making each value it's
own
column in the new data frame, and then using reshape is the answer.
Hrm.  Seems clunky.

2) Or, can a for loop around a plyr-kind of statement do the trick
(and if so, pointers on why the below code won't work) (also, it,
too,
seems clunkier than I would like)

sites<-c("a", "b", "c")
dates<-1:5

a.df<-expand.grid(sites=sites, dates=dates)
a.df$value<-runif(15,0,100)
a.df<-as.data.frame(a.df)

#now, I want to get the average of the
mean2<-function(df, date){
        sub.df<-subset(df, df$dates-date<1 &
                                df$dates-date>-1 )
        return(mean(df$value))
        }

my.df<-data.frame(sites=NA, dates=NA, V1=NA)
for(a.date in a.df$dates){
        new.df<-ddply(a.df, "sites", function(df) mean2 (df, a.date))
        my.df<-merge(my.df, new.df) #doesn't seem to work
}

my.df

Hi Folks... I've just today been re-writing some code to take
advantage of plyr (thanks for this Hadley, very logical and helpful).

I currently have some coordinates in the following object:

> str(test)
List of 2
 $ G: num [1:101, 1:2] -0.0019 -0.0019 -0.00189 -0.00188 -0.00186 ...

  .. ..$ : chr [1:2] "x.cls" "y.cls"

-0.00216 ...

  .. ..$ : NULL
  .. ..$ : chr [1:2] "x.cls" "y.cls"
 - attr(*, "split_type")= chr "data.frame"
 - attr(*, "split_labels")='data.frame':	2 obs. of  1 variable:
  ..$ group: Factor w/ 2 levels "G","T": 1 2

I want to add these coordinates to an existing plot, which I can do,
with l_ply(test, lines).  But, I want each group colored uniquely, so
I really need something like:

l_ply(test, lines, col = ????)

but I can't seem to figure out how to make col vary as I step through
the each list element.  Seems like col should be col = function(x)

color specifications).  My desired colors are in an object called
col.lvls, so I need to access it (col.lvls has the length 2 to
correspond to G and T in the case above).

I hope this is clear.  Thanks for any advice!  I'm really close to a
major clean up of code thanks to plyr.

Bryan

work, but it's hard to be absolutely sure without a reproducible
example.

messages.subject_clean: Passing ... from original function to m_ply
messages.body_plain:
Hi plyrs (I guess we are pliers, not players?):

This is an addition to a question I asked last week, where Hadley
suggested using m_plyr as follows for a plotting problem I had:

     m_ply(cbind(x = rob.coords, col = col.lvls,), lines)

which was exactly what I needed.

Now I'd like to be able to have my function, which contains the line
above, to have ... as an argument so that users can add any plotting
parameters they would like.  So for instance, my function call might
read

     myFunc(my various arguments, ...)

and I want to be able to modify my m_ply call to something like this:

    m_ply(cbind(x = rob.coords, col = col.lvls, ... = ...), lines)

or this:

    m_ply(cbind(x = rob.coords, col = col.lvls, ...), lines)

to take advantage of the additional ... arguments passed down.
However, neither of the forms above works.  I suspect I need to
capture the extra arguments in ... as a variable, then put that
variable into the m_plyr call explicitly.  If that's the case, my
question is not really about plyr; sorry if that's the case, but I bet
someone here knows the answer either way.

TIA, Bryan
***********
Prof. Bryan Hanson
Dept of Chemistry & Biochemistry
DePauw Univ
Greencastle IN USA

Here's an example of what I was talking about.  This is a routine to
generate a rolling average by site.  I know, there are functions that
will do this already, but this is a specific function that falls into
a far more general class, I think.  Also, there's a messy final NA
line in the generated data frame.  But, do you see what I am getting at?

set.seed(2003)

sites<-c("a", "b", "c")

dates<-round(runif(20,0,50))

a.df<-expand.grid(sites=sites, dates=dates)
a.df$value<-runif(30,0,100)
a.df<-as.data.frame(a.df)

#now, I want to get the average of the
mean2<-function(df, date){

	sub.df<-subset(df, df$dates-date<20 &
				df$dates-date>-20 )
	return(mean(sub.df$value))
	}

my.df<-data.frame(sites=NA, dates=NA, V1=NA)
for(a.date in a.df$dates){
	new.df<-ddply(a.df, "sites", function(df) mean2 (df, a.date))

	new.df$dates<-rep(a.date, length(new.df$V1))
	my.df<-merge(new.df, my.df, all.x=T, all.y=T) #doesn't seem to work
}

my.df

messages.body_plain:
Hi Jarrett,

Here's how I'd do.  The key is to create a generic "roll" function
that you can use with any variables.

library(ggplot2)

# Create sample data
set.seed(2003)
sites <- c("a", "b", "c")
dates <- sort(round(runif(20, 0, 50)))

df <- expand.grid(site = sites, date = dates)
df$value <- runif(30, 0, 100)

qplot(date, value, data = df, colour = site, geom = "line")

roll <- function(value, time, window, fun) {
  laply(time, function(start) {
    fun(value[abs(time - start) < window])
  })
}

df <- ddply(df, "site", transform, value.roll = roll(value, date, 5, mean))
qplot(date, value.roll, data = df, colour = site, geom = "line")

Hadley
